{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   -p RM
#   -t 48:00:00
#   -N 8
#   --ntasks-per-node 26
#   -A phy210030p
#   --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL
#   --mail-user=akshay2
#   --output=/ocean/projects/phy210030p/akshay2/Slurm_logs/multi_acceljerk_%j.log

flux alloc \
  -N 8 \
  -n 208 \
  --time=48h \
  --queue=RM \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: Slurm -A phy210030p (account/project) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but accounting/charging/allocation association may be incorrect.

# NOTE: Slurm email notifications (--mail-user/--mail-type) have no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but you will not receive BEGIN/END/FAIL emails.

# Approximate Slurm %j output naming using Flux job id.
mkdir -p /ocean/projects/phy210030p/akshay2/Slurm_logs
exec >"/ocean/projects/phy210030p/akshay2/Slurm_logs/multi_acceljerk_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.log" 2>&1

module load openmpi/3.1.6-gcc8.3.1

# Define environment variables. $PROJECT expected to be set in environment.
CMDDIR=$PROJECT/HPC_pulsar/cmd_files

# Slurm echoed $SLURM_NTASKS; approximate with requested total tasks (208).
echo 208

# Run acceleration searches.
# NOTE: This command file may internally rely on Slurm variables/launchers; no portable translation is possible here.
# Performance implication: if it expects srun/Slurm env (e.g., SLURM_NODELIST), multi-node execution may fail or underutilize resources.
$CMDDIR/multinode_accelsearch.cmd
'
"
}
